grades.quote: The need for trampoline pages could be eliminated if kernel memory were mapped into every process’s user page table (with PTE_U clear). That would also eliminate the need for a page table switch when trapping from user space into the kernel.
grades.reason: Explains that trampoline pages exist because of the user/kernel page table switch on a trap, and that mapping kernel memory into user page tables would remove the need. This is background only. It never says why the trampoline sits at the same virtual address in both tables.

grades.quote: The trampoline page. It is mapped at the top of the virtual address space; user page tables have this same mapping.
grades.reason: Confirms that the trampoline is mapped at the top of the virtual address space in both the kernel and user page tables. It defers the role of the trampoline to Chapter 4 and does not explain why the address must match.
This is only a table of contents excerpt. It has no information on the trampoline mapping.
This passage is about the page table serving as the record of allocated physical pages. It has nothing to do with the trampoline mapping.
